A.explanation: Same intensity at the sources does not guarantee same amplitude at the meeting point because amplitude falls with distance travelled.

B.explanation: Waves in phase at the point add constructively to give maximum resultant amplitude, not zero.

C.explanation: Two progressive waves can meet at an angle and still interfere, so opposite directions are not required for cancellation.

D.explanation: Equal amplitudes at the point allow a crest of one wave to exactly cancel a trough of the other when they are in antiphase.

hints: Notice the wording zero resultant amplitude at the point where the waves meet, so apply the principle of superposition of displacements at that point.
Recall that complete destructive interference needs the two displacements to be equal in size and opposite in sign at every instant, which needs antiphase plus equal magnitudes.
Compare amplitude at the point with intensity at the source, remembering amplitude can decrease with distance from different sources.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: two coherent progressive waves of the same frequency meet and superpose at one point.
State the rule: by superposition, resultant displacement $x = x_1 + x_2$ at each instant.
For the resultant to stay zero at all times, $x_2 = -x_1$, so the waves must be in antiphase at the point with displacements of equal magnitude and opposite sign.
Equal magnitude of displacement requires the same amplitude at that point, say $a$, giving $a\sin\omega t + a\sin(\omega t + \pi) = 0$.
Check the other conditions: same intensity at the sources is not enough because distances differ, in phase gives a maximum, and opposite travel directions are not needed.
Therefore equal amplitude at the meeting point must be satisfied. This is option D
